answer: A kite-maker's bamboo framing keeps Sybils out of the tundra economy. A newcomer frames 16 kites over 24 days. Two kite-makers from different yards measure each kite's bamboo spars, flight-test it, and log it on the kite board. One kite that will not hold steady in wind voids its credit and freezes rewards 14 days; three failed kites void the whole tally. Faking 1,000 agents means 16,000 kites and 32,000 tests: $240,000 in cedar spars and 96,000 hours of skilled labor, while one honest agent flies its kites. Trust here is nectar, gathered slowly, drop by drop, impossible to fake in bulk.
